tagline: Bluff roads and a dam crossing link the Susquehanna’s river ports
intro: The Lower Susquehanna Scenic Byway links Perryville and Havre de Grace over 33 miles, climbing above Port Deposit and crossing the river atop Conowingo Dam. Maryland’s tourism office highlights river views, waterfront history and birding along this state scenic route, with a driving time of one to two hours. On the western side, Susquehanna State Park brings heavy forest cover and large rock outcrops into the journey. The western route alternates between riverside Stafford Road and an inland stretch following Deer Creek, rather than tracing the bank throughout.

The crossing changed when Conowingo Dam was built. Its reservoir would have submerged the existing U.S. Route 1 bridge, which was demolished in 1927; the highway now runs over the dam. The project also required the railroad to move to higher ground and displaced the original town of Conowingo. The hydroelectric project was completed in 1928.

From Perryville, head toward Port Deposit on the east bank, where older buildings occupy the narrow ground between river and bluffs. Continue north to Conowingo Dam and cross on U.S. 1. On the west side, the byway reaches Susquehanna State Park before continuing to Havre de Grace. Finish beside the waterfront promenade and restored Concord Point Lighthouse.

moments.title: Port Deposit
moments.text: Port Deposit’s older buildings fit into a narrow strip between the Susquehanna and the bluffs, with terraces and stairs connecting streets above. Its position once made it a transfer point: cargo coming downriver could be loaded onto Chesapeake ships here and at Lapidum, the northernmost navigable deepwater ports. Local quarries supplied the stone commonly called Port Deposit granite, actually gneiss, used in many town buildings. Many residences date to the early 1800s, part of the built waterfront encountered on the byway’s eastern side. From Main Street, a brick-and-stone staircase climbs 75 steps above town to a view of four river bridges.
moments.notice: Look for the stone buildings and stairs rising between the riverfront streets and terraced bluffs.

moments.title: Conowingo Dam
moments.text: U.S. 1 crosses the top of Conowingo Dam, replacing a bridge demolished before the reservoir filled. Philadelphia Electric Company commissioned the project; Stone & Webster designed it, and Maryland’s Arundel Corporation carried out construction beginning in 1926. The reservoir covers the original town of Conowingo, which was moved during construction. The dam was completed in 1928. Construction reshaped the transport corridor as well as the river: the Columbia and Port Deposit Railroad was moved to a higher elevation. At Fisherman’s Wharf & Park, hawks, great blue herons and bald eagles are often seen along the river.

moments.title: Havre de Grace
moments.text: The waterfront promenade leads to Concord Point Lighthouse where the Susquehanna meets the Chesapeake Bay. Hurricane Isabel destroyed the promenade in September 2003. It was rebuilt in 2004 with help from AmeriCorps NCCC and again connects Tydings Park, the Maritime Museum and the lighthouse. Elsewhere on the waterfront, the restored lock house preserves another transport story. Havre de Grace was the southern end of the Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal, built to bypass difficult river navigation between here and Wrightsville, Pennsylvania. The lock keeper’s house and canal remnants form a museum.
